==Problem==
What value of <imath>x</imath> satisfies
<cmath>x- \frac{3}{4} = \frac{5}{12} - \frac{1}{3}?</cmath>
<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ {-}\frac{2}{3}\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ \frac{7}{36}\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ \frac{7}{12}\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ \frac{2}{3}\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ \frac{5}{6}</imath>

== Solution 1 == 

Adding <imath>\frac{3}{4}</imath> to both sides, <imath>x= \frac{5}{12} - \frac{1}{3} + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{5}{12} - \frac{4}{12} + \frac{9}{12}=\boxed{\textbf{(E) }\frac{5}{6}}</imath>.

==Solution 2==
Multiplying <imath>12</imath> on both sides gets us <imath>12x-9=1 \Rightarrow 12x=10</imath>, therefore <imath>x=\boxed{\textbf{(E)}~\frac{5}{6}}</imath>.
